guide.title: Prague: A Free Fairy Tale 3 Day Itinerary
guide.description:
Prague is one of Europe’s most enchanting capitals, where medieval charm meets
a rich and resilient history. It’s an easy city that is easy to explore on foot (or you
can buy a multi day transit pass),  fi lled with stunning architecture, vibrant
squares, and unforgettable views.

data.name: Old Town Square
data.description: Old Town Square, located in the heart of Prague, is a historic public square surrounded by stunning Gothic and Baroque buildings. Notable landmarks include the iconic Astronomical Clock, Týn Church, and St. Nicholas Church. The square has been a focal point of city life since the 12th century, hosting various events, markets, and celebrations. Its cobblestone streets and vibrant atmosphere attract both locals and tourists alike, o ff ering a glimpse into the rich history and culture of the Czech Republic. It's an ideal place for leisurely walks, dining, and exploring local shops.

data.name: Prague Astronomical Clock
data.description: The Prague Astronomical Clock, or Prague Orloj, is a medieval astronomical clock mounted on the southern wall of the Old Town Hall in Prague's Old Town Square. Installed in 1410, it is the third-oldest astronomical clock in the world and the oldest still in operation. The clock features an astronomical dial, a calendar dial, and hourly shows with moving  fi gures, including the Twelve Apostles and a skeleton representing Death. Tips If you take a walking tour they will actually teach you what the clock represents which was really valuable for enjoying the "show"

data.name: The Powder Tower
data.description: The Powder Tower, also known as the Cosmas and Damian Tower, is a Gothic tower in Prague that dates back to the 15th century. It served as one of the original city gates and is a striking example of medieval architecture. Standing 65 meters tall, the tower features intricate carvings and sculptures, making it a popular attraction for visitors. Today, tourists can climb its stairs for panoramic views of the city, experiencing a blend of history and culture in the heart of Prague. Today's Eats

data.name: Terasa U Prince
data.description: Czechia +420 739 609 779 Terasa U Prince is an open-air restaurant situated on the rooftop of the historic Hotel U Prince, overlooking the stunning Old Town Square in Prague. Guests can enjoy a sophisticated dining experience with a breathtaking panoramic view of iconic landmarks such as the Astronomical Clock and St. Nicholas Church. The restaurant specializes in a blend of traditional Czech cuisine and contemporary dishes, creating a unique menu that caters to various palates. Its atmospheric setting makes it a popular choice for both locals and tourists seeking a memorable meal in an enchanting location. Tips I suggest making a reservation online as this place is a popular spot. The views are phenomenal including the photo spot, but it is de fi nitely tourist pricing.

data.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
data.description: St. Vitus Cathedral, a stunning example of Gothic architecture, is located within the Prague Castle complex. This iconic cathedral, founded in 934, serves as the burial site of Bohemian kings and the seat of the Archbishop of Prague. Its breathtaking stained glass windows and intricate spires attract millions of visitors each year. The cathedral's many chapels and artworks showcase centuries of artistry and religious signi fi cance, making it a must-visit for those exploring the city's rich history and culture.

data.name: Prague Castle
data.description: Prague Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is an iconic symbol of the Czech Republic, boasting a rich history that dates back to the 9th century. It is one of the largest ancient castles in the world, with stunning architectural styles ranging from Romanesque to Gothic. Within its walls, visitors can explore the grand St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and beautiful gardens, all while enjoying panoramic views of the city. The castle complex is not only a signi fi cant historical site but also a cultural hub, hosting various art exhibitions and events throughout the year.

data.name: Lesser Quarter (Mala Strana)
data.description: Lesser Quarter (Malá Strana) is one of Prague's oldest districts, located just below Prague Castle. Renowned for its charming streets and historic buildings, it features remarkable sites such as St. Nicholas Church and the John Lennon Wall. This picturesque area is characterized by its Baroque structures, peaceful gardens, and vibrant artistic atmosphere. Visitors can explore quaint cafes, shops, and galleries nestled among the narrow alleyways, creating a unique blend of history and culture. The district serves as a gateway to the picturesque Vltava River and o ff ers stunning views of the city and the iconic Charles Bridge. Today's Eats Piknik Park Italian Nosticova 470/8, Malá Strana, 118 00 Praha-Praha 1, Czechia +420 601 164 711 Piknik Park is an authentic Italian restaurant located on Kampa Island in Prague's Malá Strana district, just a two- minute walk from the Charles Bridge and near the Lennon Wall. The restaurant features a private, year-round heated terrace overlooking the Čertovka River, often referred to as 'Little Prague Venice.' The menu o ff ers a wide selection of quality Czech wines complemented by premium international wines. The open kitchen is run by top local chefs, ensuring fresh and high-quality dishes. The restaurant has been featured in The Guardian and has received over 250  fi ve-star reviews in 21 di ff erent languages. Tips Gluten free pizza was delicious! data.name: Gingerbread Man
data.description: The Gingerbread Man is a bakery and cafe located in Prague, Czechia, known for its gingerbread. The aroma of gingerbread often draws people in, and the shop o ff ers many choices, including di ff erent shapes and sizes. Some customers have found the taste average and the texture slightly dry, while others enjoyed the balance of  fl avors. Many recommend it for its smell and selection of packaged goods suitable as gifts. The shop is often crowded, and fresh gingerbread is constantly being baked. Tips No gluten free options when I visited, but it smells delicious and the people I was traveling with enjoyed it!

data.name: Maisel Synagogue (Maiselova Synagoga)
data.description: Maisel Synagogue, located in the Jewish Quarter of Prague, is a remarkable example of Gothic architecture. Built in the late 16th century, it was initially constructed as a place of worship for the Jewish community. The synagogue now houses a museum that chronicles the history of Jews in the Czech lands. Its stunning interior features intricate details, including beautiful stained glass windows and preserved artifacts, o ff ering visitors a glimpse into Jewish heritage. The synagogue plays a vital role in the cultural landscape of Prague, attracting tourists and historians alike.

data.name: Pinkas Synagogue
data.description: The Pinkas Synagogue, established in 1535, is one of the oldest synagogues in Prague and serves as a poignant Holocaust memorial. It is part of the Jewish Museum in Prague and is dedicated to the memory of the nearly 80,000 Jewish victims from Bohemia and Moravia who perished during the Holocaust. The synagogue's walls are inscribed with the names of these victims, making it a powerful site of remembrance. Additionally, the synagogue houses a collection of children's drawings from the Terezín ghetto, o ff ering a glimpse into the lives and hopes of young Jewish children during World War II.

data.name: Spanish Synagogue
data.description: The Spanish Synagogue, located in the heart of Prague, is an exquisite example of Moorish Revival architecture. Completed in 1883, it features intricate details, vibrant stained glass windows, and a stunning interior that re fl ects Jewish heritage and culture. The synagogue serves as a place of worship and a museum, showcasing the rich history of Jewish communities in the Czech Republic. Visitors can explore its beautiful prayer hall and learn about its historical signi fi cance, making it a must-visit destination for those interested in architecture and history. Today's Eats

data.name: Next Door by Imperial
data.description: Next Door by Imperial is a modern Czech bistro located at Zlatnická 3 in Prague. The restaurant features an open kitchen where guests can observe chefs preparing dishes with seasonal ingredients and re fi ned techniques. Under the guidance of Chef Zdeněk Pohlreich, the culinary team creates fresh, decorated cakes daily, maintaining traditional Czech pastry methods while incorporating modern presentation techniques. The establishment operates under Chef Zdeněk Pohlreich's guidance, who has shaped Czech gastronomy through his culinary expertise and restaurant ventures. The restaurant accepts reservations for groups up to twenty people and maintains a non-smoking policy. It serves breakfast from 7 AM, o ff ering specialized morning menus that cater to both business meetings and family gatherings.
